key_insight: Reward models must be evaluated not only for overall quality but for how well they reflect individual user preferences; Personalized RewardBench provides a targeted benchmark to measure RM performance on human-aligned personalization.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of standardized evaluation for whether reward models capture diverse, individual user preferences (pluralistic alignment) rather than only aggregate or average preferences.
method: Curate/label preference data tied to distinct user profiles or preference personas to represent pluralistic human values.
Define an evaluation protocol and metrics that measure personalization fidelity (e.g., per-user ranking accuracy, consistency, and robustness) alongside general quality metrics.
Benchmark a range of reward models under controlled personalization scenarios to reveal trade-offs between global alignment and individualized alignment.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical tool to diagnose and compare reward models on personalization ability, guiding model selection and RM training strategies to improve user satisfaction and safer, more human-aligned LLM behavior.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data collection → persona creation → RM scoring → per-person evaluation metrics
Heatmap or matrix: RM scores (rows) vs. user personas (columns) to show personalization strengths/weaknesses
Bar chart: comparison of personalization metrics (e.g., per-user accuracy, consistency) across several reward models
Icon set: user-persona icons, reward function icon, and alignment/safety shield to convey goals at a glance
paper_title: Personalized RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models with Human Aligned Personalization
paper_authors: Qiyao Ma, Dechen Gao, Rui Cai, Boqi Zhao, Hanchu Zhou
